sections.skill: Prove that the elimination step keeps the same solutions

questions.skill: Prove that the elimination step keeps the same solutions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: System A: x + y = 9 and x - y = 3. System B: x + y = 9 and 2x = 12 (its second equation is the sum of the two equations of A). Show that every solution of A is a solution of B, and every solution of B is a solution of A.
questions.prompt_markup:
System A: x + y = 9 and x - y = 3.
System B: x + y = 9 and 2x = 12 (its second equation is the sum of the two equations of A).
Show that every solution of A is a solution of B, and every solution of B is a solution of A.
questions.correct_answer: The systems have the same solutions; both have only (6, 3).
questions.required_method: Both directions are required. A to B: if (x, y) makes both equations of A true, adding them gives 2x = 12, so (x, y) solves B. B to A: if (x, y) solves B, subtracting x + y = 9 from 2x = 12 gives x - y = 3, so (x, y) solves A.

questions.skill: Prove that the elimination step keeps the same solutions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: System A: x + 2y = 7 and -3x + y = 0. Replace the second equation by its sum with 3 times the first equation. Write the new system, and show how to get the original second equation back from it.
questions.prompt_markup:
System A: x + 2y = 7 and -3x + y = 0. Replace the second equation by its sum with 3 times the first equation.
Write the new system, and show how to get the original second equation back from it.
questions.correct_answer: New system: x + 2y = 7 and 7y = 21. Subtracting 3(x + 2y) = 21 from 7y = 21 gives -3x + y = 0 again.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the new system and the reverse step.

questions.skill: Prove that the elimination step keeps the same solutions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Why does replacing one equation by its sum with a multiple of the other keep the same solutions?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does replacing one equation by its sum with a multiple of the other keep the same solutions?

choices.text: Adding equations always gives the solution directly.
The new equation always describes the same line as the old one.
Multiplying an equation by a number changes its graph.
The step can be undone by subtracting the same multiple, so no solution is gained or lost.

questions.correct_answer: The step can be undone by subtracting the same multiple, so no solution is gained or lost.
